summary: Soft-pion spectra and hybrid-model calibration, critical-point femtoscopy, and statistically validated stochastic-trajectory surrogates dominate the latest announced batch. The selected papers were submitted on 13 November, outside the strict 24-hour window.

papers.title: Are hybrid hydrodynamic models missing soft-pion physics?
papers.short_authors: Osvaldo Ferreira, Thiago S. Domingues, Fernando G. Gardim, et al.
papers.summary: A Bayesian analysis of a hybrid hydrodynamic model finds a low-pT pion excess relative to ALICE data that is not shared by kaons or protons. Two one-parameter enhancement templates are tested; the infrared template improves the calibration and mean-pT agreement.
papers.abstract: The authors scan the hybrid-model parameter space, confirm a low-pT pion excess even with a hadronic afterburner, examine centrality scaling and test two candidate enhancement mechanisms.
papers.why_it_matters: Soft-pion discrepancies can bias extraction of medium parameters and point toward missing late-stage physics.
papers.assessment: A careful model-data study with a broad parameter analysis and an afterburner. The fitted templates do not identify a unique microscopic cause; conclusions remain conditional on the model, priors, and data treatment.

papers.title: Searching for signatures of criticality in heavy-ion collisions using two-pion correlation functions
papers.short_authors: Alejandro Ayala, Santiago Bernal-Langarica, Máté Csanád, et al.
papers.summary: EPOS simulations with a critical-point equation of state examine Lévy-fitted two-pion sources in Bi+Bi collisions at 5.8–11 GeV. The authors find no unambiguous critical signature; resonance contributions may affect the intercept trend.
papers.abstract: The study fits simulated pair-distance distributions and momentum correlations to Lévy forms across collision energies using an equation of state containing a critical endpoint.
papers.why_it_matters: It tests a proposed experimental critical-point observable and illustrates an important background.
papers.assessment: A useful cautionary feasibility study, not evidence for or against a critical point. A matched no-critical-point baseline and varied critical strength are needed to establish sensitivity.

papers.title: Learning and Generating Time Trajectories of Multidimensional Stochastic Processes
papers.short_authors: Zihan Xu, Changho Kim, Andy J. Nonaka, Yuanran Zhu
papers.summary: A noise-driven recurrent network learns joint statistics using projected distributions and adaptive loss balancing. It is tested on coupled Duffing dynamics, a Fermi–Pasta–Ulam chain and a lattice kinetic Monte Carlo model, with finite-sample-normalized validation.
papers.abstract: The paper extends statistics-informed neural networks to multidimensional processes and studies projected distributions, adaptive training, noise dimension, and statistical validation across three stochastic benchmarks.
papers.why_it_matters: A possible surrogate for ensembles of coupled Langevin trajectories in heavy-quark transport or fluctuating hydrodynamics, subject to domain-specific validation.
papers.assessment: Methodologically interesting with several benchmarks, but no heavy-ion demonstration. Finite projections can miss joint or rare-event structure; conservation, uncertainty, tails, speed and out-of-distribution robustness require dedicated testing.
